newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-QB MOON AGREES TO TWO-YEAR DEAL WITH SEAHAWKS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-QB MOON AGREES TO TWO-YEAR DEAL WITH SEAHAWKS.

text.p: Eight-time Pro Bowl quarterback Warren Moon, who was released by the Minnesota Vikings after refusing to take a pay cut, Friday agreed to a two-year deal with the Seattle Seahawks.
Financial terms were not disclosed, but Moon reportedly rejected a two-year, $1.5 million offer from the San Diego Chargers to sign with Seattle.
Had Moon gone with San Diego he would have been reunited with Kevin Gilbride, the Chargers new head coach who was Moon's offensive coordinator with the Houston Oilers.
Playing for the Seahawks will be something of a homecoming for Moon, who attended college at the University of Washington.

Seattle was seeking a veteran backup to quarterback John Friesz after trading Rick Mirer to Chicago. Moon is the Seahawks' fourth major free agent signing, joining linebacker Chad Brown, safety Bennie Blades and cornerback Willie Williams.
The 40-year-old Moon was released by the Vikings February 21, less than four months after signing a three-year, $15 million contract extension with the team.
He struggled through an injury-plagued 1996 campaign and Brad Johnson took over as the Vikings' starter, leading them to the playoffs.
In December the Vikings rewarded Johnson with a four-year, $15 million deal and asked Moon to take a major pay cut, which he refused.
Moon, who played three years for the Vikings, completed just over 54 percent of his passes last season for 1,610 yards with seven touchdowns and nine interceptions.

He is fourth on the National Football League's all-time list in passing yards (43,569) and completions (3,514). Moon began his pro career in the Canadian Football League, playing six seasons with the Edmonton Eskimos before leading the Houston Oilers for 10 seasons.
Moon was named to the Pro Bowl eight consecutive seasons before 1996.

In 1995, he posted his eighth 3,000-yard passing season, tying him with Joe Montana for third on the NFL's all-time list. He has surpassed the 4,000-yard single-season passing mark four times, putting him second behind Dan Marino's six.
